analysis.title: Weekly Economic Roundup (23 November 2026)
key_insights: PNC sees the main economic risk running through equities, since a large decline hits both wealth-driven consumer spending and AI-driven capex (a 'two-birds-one-stone' shock).
The S&P 500 fell as much as 11% from its prior peak and the Nasdaq nearly 20%, a 'growth scare' move with declines in oil, gold and copper and wider credit spreads.
Rule of thumb: each 10% equity decline shaves about 0.3pp off annual real GDP growth. A sustained 10% drop would lower consensus 2027 real GDP growth from 2.2% to 1.9%, still near potential.

Risks scale nonlinearly once declines reach 20% or more, as odds of a self-reinforcing recessionary spiral rise. PNC also needs evidence of slowing growth and ebbing corporate profits, which it does not see yet.
PNC expects the Fed to still hike in December and thinks the equity selloff alone is highly unlikely to dissuade it. A continued selloff would more likely lower hike odds for January and March.
October PCE price index due Wednesday 11/25: PNC expects headline and core both +0.3% M/M, with core rising from 3.1% to around 3.2% Y/Y, reinforcing that price pressures are too strong for the Fed.
Other data this week include new home sales (PNC 650k vs 676k prior), durable goods, Q3 GDP second estimate (PNC 3.5% vs 3.4% prior), claims, the Beige Book, and the advance goods trade balance.

tension_points.bull_case: A 10% equity decline shaves only 0.3pp from growth, taking 2027 GDP from 2.2% to 1.9%, and underlying growth and profits remain strong.
tension_points.bear_case: Risks scale nonlinearly at 20% or more declines, with self-reinforcing spirals and hits to both consumer spending and AI capex.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Equity decline of 20% or more coupled with evidence of slowing growth and ebbing corporate profits.
